Sam K: Handoff for 11:00–19:00 PT today — I'm taking over now. Quick question: if we see a sudden drop in KV cache hit rate (>15% drop), who triages first, runtime or SRE? Also what's the escalation path if it becomes customer-impacting?

Maria G: Short answer: runtime owns model/runtime cache logic and regressions. SRE owns infra (hosts, network, GPUs) and pager routing. If it's a cache logic bug (e.g., wrong keys, prefixing), runtime. If it's nodes OOM/evictions or network issues causing cache pressure, SRE.

Sam K: Got it. How are we defining an "incident" for this kind of degradation? Any thresholds?

Devon: From runbook (TL;DR): incident = any state causing sustained user-facing errors or an SLO breach. Practically: sustained error rate or latency SLO breach (>5% SLO miss) for 5+ minutes -> treat as incident. For cache drops alone: P1 if it leads to errors or >20% latency increase; otherwise P2 and handle async.

Devon: ```runbook
Incident definitions (summary):
- P0: total outage or data loss
- P1: sustained user-facing errors or SLO breach >5 minutes
- P2: degraded performance/quality, requires coordinated async response
- P3: informational/ops tasks
```

Alex P: Escalation flow we use: oncall -> SRE lead -> Runtime lead -> Eng manager. Note: infra pager pages SRE team directly; runtime regressions page runtime oncall. If unsure, page the oncall channel first and follow the runbook escalate steps (there's an `/escalate` bookmark in the runbook).

oncall-bot: Reminder: Sam K is now oncall for #eng-oncall (11:00 PT -> 19:00 PT). Rotation ID: 172. If you need a shadow, DM Alex P.

Maria G: For handoffs please leave a short note in /handovers and update the oncall notes doc with current KV hit rates + any anomalies. Quick links: metrics dashboard (1h/5m views) -> https://redwood.internal/metrics/kv-hit

Sam K: Will update the handover doc now. One more: if we suspect a model-level quality regression (not infra), do we page ML folks or runtime first?

Maria G: Model-level quality -> page Runtime oncall first. Runtime will confirm and open a ticket to ML (or call ML lead) if it's a model regression. Only page SRE if there are infra symptoms (OOMs, node restarts, network errors).

Sam K: Thanks, that helps. I'll annotate the handoff notes with current KV hit % and recent error spikes, and ping runtime if alerts cross P1 thresholds.

Sam K: @Devon can you add a short flow diagram to the runbook that maps: cache drop -> triage path (runtime vs SRE) + example pager messages?

Devon: On it — will add flow + sample pager commands by EOD today :+1:

Alex P: Also adding: if you need to escalate outside hours, follow the emergency contact list in the runbook (mobile numbers). Keep pages concise: include metric links, `grep` log sample, and recent deploy id. Example: `P1 - KV hit drop -> 2024-07-10 11:12 UTC -> dashboard link -> recent deploy: gke-rw-2024-07-09-rc3`

Sam K: Perfect. Logging my handoff note now and adding the 5m/1h graphs. Ping me in-thread if you add the runbook diagram so I can link it.

Maria G: Thanks — appreciate the handoff.
